items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: Chico then did “Sweet Smell of Success” with the group... I could bring my group but in order to get a big crowd you’d do better with the Chico Hamilton quintet because the band never got to Europe when we were playing before.

ctx.x: And he brought his book, so then when I came to join them they were playing basically Bob’s arrangements. I brought a couple of charts of my own. And then Fred would actually play just cello solos on intermission. Because of that great energy he had. He wouldn’t take a break. Chico would say, “You want to do some cello playing?” He said yeah he’d do “Granada” and a lot of solos. But then what he’d finally do, he’d play too long and Chico was anxious to get back on the stand, especially if we had a packed house.…

items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: one of my early groups, when Buddy Collette left the group... his band mates included Buddy Collette

ctx.x: Were blacks and whites allowed to play together?

Oh yeah. As a matter of fact, oh yeah. Out in L.A. anyway. I don’t know about the rest of the country because I didn’t leave L.A. until I was about 21 I think, something like that. But to my knowledge, as a matter of fact, one of my early groups, when Buddy Collette left the group, Paul Horn joined the group, right? And I was billed as Chico Hamilton and his All White Orchestra.

items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I ended up being the drummer with the group and that’s how we virtually in a sense got started.

ctx.x: Stay in school. He told me to stay in school, you know, and that was cool. So in the meantime, Lee was playing with Lorenzo Flennoy and they were playing at the Club Alabam, which was the number one club there, which was equivalent to the Cotton Club here in New York. They had a line of girls, chorus line, singers, dancers, and entertainers, you know, comedians, and I started subbing for Lee playing the show. In the meantime our band that we used to have, we took a gig at the Follies and Buddy, myself, Jack,…
Sing that pattern, the kick pattern for the strippers.
